gate.ask.verbal:
[OwnMind] 🟢 The AI wants to do something your rules say to ask about first, so OwnMind stopped it: {title}
  Reply "go" and OwnMind allows it this once; reply "no" and it does not.
gate.ask.code.action:
[OwnMind] 🟢 The AI wants to do something your rules say to ask about first, so OwnMind stopped it: {title}
  Paste this number to the AI and OwnMind allows it this once: {code}
gate.ask.code.limit:
[OwnMind] 🟡 OwnMind has blocked the same command from the AI 3 times and it is still trying. It is stuck on this rule: {title}
  Paste this number to the AI and OwnMind allows it this once: {code}. If you would rather it stopped, just ignore this.
gate.read.blocked:
[OwnMind] 🟢 The AI tried to act without reading this rule first, so OwnMind stopped it: {title}
  Once the AI has read the rule and retried, OwnMind lets it through automatically. Nothing for you to do.
gate.check.blocked:
[OwnMind] 🟢 The AI's command does not meet your rules, so OwnMind stopped it: {reason}
  Once the AI fixes the command and retries it will go through. Nothing for you to do.
gate.failopen: [OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind could not check this command, and the AI ran it anyway. If it matters, look at what it did.
gate.degraded: [OwnMind] 🟡 OwnMind could not confirm whether the AI had read your rules this time, but it is still blocking the AI's commands against them.
lint.recovered: [OwnMind] 🟢 OwnMind checked the AI's reply against your rules (checking had been down, it is back).
lint.offReminder:
[OwnMind v{version}] 🔴 OwnMind is off, and {tick} of the AI's replies have skipped the reply-quality check.
  → To turn it back on: type /ownmind-on, or just start a new conversation.
lint.banner.header.downgraded: [OwnMind v{version}] 🟡 The AI's reply went back for a rewrite {blockCount} times and still is not right, so OwnMind has stopped sending it back and is showing it to you. Your call whether to accept it.
lint.banner.header.blocked: [OwnMind v{version}] 🟢 The AI's reply breaks your rules, so OwnMind has told the AI to rewrite it ({count} so far in this conversation).
lint.banner.header.blockMode: [OwnMind v{version}] 🟢 OwnMind found something in the AI's reply that breaks your rules ({count} so far in this conversation). {remaining} more and OwnMind will tell the AI to rewrite it.
lint.banner.header.otherMode: [OwnMind v{version}] 🟡 OwnMind found something in the AI's reply that breaks your rules ({count} so far in this conversation). For now OwnMind only warns; it does not ask for a rewrite.
lint.banner.modeInvalid: 🔴 OwnMind does not recognise the reply-check setting '{rawMode}', so this run only warns and asks for no rewrite.
compliance.off.warnMode: [OwnMind] 🟡 In this conversation OwnMind only warns; it never asks the AI to rewrite.
compliance.notChecked.noCredentials: [OwnMind] 🔴 This computer is not signed in to OwnMind, so OwnMind did not check the AI's reply.
compliance.notChecked.neverSynced: [OwnMind] 🔴 This computer has not downloaded your rules yet, so OwnMind did not check the AI's reply. Start a new conversation and it will fetch them.
compliance.notChecked.signedOut: [OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind does not recognise this computer any more, so OwnMind did not check the AI's reply. You need to sign in again: run the install command again with new sign-in details.
compliance.notChecked.judgeNotStarted: [OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind could not start checking the AI's reply, so this reply was not checked against your rules. Re-running the OwnMind update script usually repairs it.
compliance.off.server: [OwnMind] 🔴 Rule checking is switched off for your account, so OwnMind did not check the AI's reply.
compliance.idNote: (if OwnMind got it wrong, reply 誤判 {checkId})
gate.allow.verbal:
[OwnMind] 🟡 The AI said you agreed to 「{title}」, so OwnMind allowed it this once.
  If you did say so, ignore this; if you did not, stop it now.
gate.ask.forged:
[OwnMind] 🟡 The AI had an approval on file for this that OwnMind did not issue.
  OwnMind ignored it and is asking you instead.
gate.ask.unverifiable:
[OwnMind] 🟡 There is an approval on file for this and OwnMind cannot tell whether it issued it.
  OwnMind did not use it, and is asking you instead. Re-running the OwnMind update script repairs this.
gate.ask.notRecorded:
[OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind could not save this approval, so it will not recognise your answer.
  Re-running the OwnMind update script repairs this.
verdict.notChecked:
[OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind could not check one of the AI's earlier replies, so that reply was not checked against your rules.
  Re-running the OwnMind update script usually repairs it; until then nothing is checking the AI against your rules.
verdict.violation:
[OwnMind] 🟡 OwnMind checked one of the AI's earlier replies and it breaks {count} of your rules, starting with {title}
  OwnMind has passed this to the AI, which should correct itself from here. This is a reminder, not a block: OwnMind cannot make it comply, so check that it did.
verdict.notChecked.noCli:
[OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind checks the AI's replies by asking Claude Code on this computer, and it could not find it, so that reply was not checked.
  Install Claude Code on this computer and make sure typing claude in a terminal starts it.
verdict.didNotFinish:
[OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind started checking one of the AI's replies and never heard back, so that reply was not checked against your rules.
  The next reply is checked from scratch. If this keeps happening, run the OwnMind update script.
verdict.recovered: [OwnMind] 🟢 OwnMind is checking the AI's replies against your rules again.
verdict.notChecked.notLoggedIn:
[OwnMind] 🔴 Claude Code on this computer is not signed in, so OwnMind could not have it check the AI's reply.
  Sign in to Claude Code again and checking comes back on its own.
verdict.notChecked.cliRefused:
[OwnMind] 🔴 OwnMind asked Claude Code on this computer to check the AI's reply and it would not, so that reply was not checked.
  Try running claude yourself in a terminal: whatever it says there is what OwnMind ran into.
